newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares ease, prospects seen uncertain.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares ease, prospects seen uncertain.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased 0.67 percent on Monday on low turnover, as investors increasingly turned their attention to shares of newly privatised companies that yet have to be listed on the market, traders said.

"Most of the trading is going on in unlisted shares of newly privatised companies. Only after these shares are listed or when fresh foreign capital enters the market can we expect situation on the market to improve," Karmen Korbun, a trader at Creditanstalt, said.
* The seven-share SBI index fell 6.45 points to 975.88.
* Five shares fell and 11 rose, while seven were untraded.
* Turnover fell to 37.9 million tolars from 45.2 million.
* Pharmaceutical wholesaler Salus was the most actively traded issue and the biggest gainer, firming 7.75 percent to 13,687 tolars on volume of 1,010 shares for total turnover of 13.8 million tolars.

* Common shares of brokerage Nika were the leading decliner, falling 3.21 percent to 3,775 tolars on volume of 67 shares for total turnover of 253,000 tolars. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
